Perfume rating 4.05 out of 5 with 4,580 votes

Dia Woman by Amouage is a Floral fragrance for women. Dia Woman was launched in 2002. The nose behind this fragrance is Jean-Claude Ellena. Top notes are Aldehydes, Cyclamen, Violet Leaf, Bergamot, Sage, Tarragon and Fig; middle notes are Peony, Turkish Rose Oil, Orris Root, Orange Blossom and Peach Blossom; base notes are White Musk, Heliotrope, Sandalwood, Incense, Cedar, Vanilla and Guaiac Wood.

Dia is a luxury scent for day wear, that is both sophisticated and vibrant. A lighter day version to be a perfect compliment to Amouage Gold which is intended for evening.
The distinctive bottles are made from 24% French lead crystal embellished with pink gold.

The top note includes fig, cyclamen, bergamot, tarragon, sage and violet leaves. Heart is of precious and fresh flowers: peach blossom, rose oil, orange flower, peony and orris. The dry down is woodsy oriental and rich, consists of white musk, misterious incense, vanilla, heliotrope, cedarwood, sandalwood and Guaiac wood.
The perfume was created by Jean-Claude Ellena in 2002.

luvoxlixir 03/30/25 22:33

Dia is the deceptive smell of a powder puff left too long in the sun. A burst of aldehydes, crisp and effervescent, starts the theme airy, celestial even—but then, it sinks. Powdery warmth thickens, dense like finely milled talc, but with a shadow creeping through: a touch of animalic skank. That unmistakable Amouage musk, lurking. Baby powder, yes, but aged, filthy. And laced with something so off.

The rose, meant to be delicate, carries an unexpected weight—fruit-tinged, heady, almost overripe. It clings, unfurling with a vintage languor that feels more claustrophobic than refined. I know there DNA... I should have seen this coming. There’s a moment of hesitation—perhaps it will lift, bloom, redeem itself—but no. It settles, unwavering, into its powdered throne. Oh so auffocating in a cloud of old-world excess. No thank you.

LadyIva 05/11/24 11:17

I haven't worn Dia in a few years; I allowed it to macerate, to see if its longevity would improve. And guess what - it did! Now I get 8 hours easily. The opening is in the style of Arab perfumery - powdery spicy rose with incense, strong musk and sparkling aldehydes. Depending on your taste, it might smell slightly dated or dusty. But even if you don't like the opening, just let this perfume sit on your skin for about an hour, and then you won't be able to stop sniffing your wrists! It is *that* beautiful and enchanting. Jean-Claude Ellena's mastery is revealed in the fact that he can make a complex perfume with a myriad of notes appear transparent, effortless, classy and entirely office-appropriate - although this one can be worn on any occasion, from high-society weddings to date nights. In any case, Dia requires a mature wearer, probably a 30+ professional woman, because it is the exact opposite of mainstream kiddie-friendly pinkish juices. I would classify Dia as a floral woody musk, because that's the direction the scent takes after the aldehydes evaporate. Now off to sniff my wrists. :)

This is more of a comparison letter to myself than it is a review for someone else. Right now I have on Dia and I just sprayed it less than 10 minutes ago. Lots of aldehyde and other clean notes that are perfectly balanced. I'm not the biggest fan of this note pyramid but I like it here. It's not too much. It is clean but not too clean. Course we all think of Chanel. I can tell you right now I don't like that brand identity whatsoever. I have the jersey and that's it. So me personally, I think aldehyde is the least sexy fragrance note you can possibly put on. I don't connect the dots. It smells like you either got out of the shower or you just cleaned the kitchen. My brain does not formulate any attractive, sensual, exciting moments when I apply something that has aldehyde in it. However, you don't always have to have that element when you are wearing something. In this specific scenario, Dia is a wonderful offering if you are looking for something very professional, clean, elegant, perhaps even informative. This is a fragrance not associated with a younger woman. There is no fruity or vanilla or anything of that sort. Complete disassociation from that. And I'm here for it! There is something refreshing about it just because everything that has come out recently is either vanilla or some kind of sweet, spicy, a mixture of the two, or something else along those lines. Maybe you could say this is old-school. Yes you could probably say that. However, I don't consider that a negative here. If you let it sit, which is what I'm doing right now, the aldehyde starts to fade, and white blossoms start to emerge as well as a very gentle sweetness. All of a sudden it becomes 20 years younger. And this is some kind of an art form other fragrance houses simply cannot get right or even compete with whatsoever. I mention this all the time but I'll say it again. Don't make a judgment from Amouage until you have let it sit on your skin for at least six hours. Every single fragrance from their entire line transitions into something extraordinary. Dia starts at one point and ends up in an entirely different point. Not everyone likes aldehyde, especially myself, but I'll be damned if anyone says the dry down is not exceptional.

Jloveparfum 06/06/22 22:53

"SMELL IS A WORD, PERFUME IS LITERATURE ”
Jean-Claude Ellena.

I am fascinated by Amouage creations because each one of them tells a unique story and has a distinctive character. However, they all share the same seal of luxury and exclusivity that characterizes The Maison.

DIA is an aldehydic floral fragrance that dazzles with its beauty and sophistication. It has an air of a classic French perfume but at the same time it is modern, innocent and youthful compared to others from this house. Although it may remind you of the iconic Chanel N5 for its sparkling and soapy output, Día has its own personality that is revealed in its evolution. Its aldehydic notes are of exceptional quality, vibrant and fresh, but also delicate and elegant.

The fragrance begins with a green, fresh and clean accord that captivates from the first moment. Then it becomes sweeter and more floral in the heart, a bouquet of white and pink flowers, which provide sweetness and sensuality. Rose and iris blend harmoniously with fruity and spicy accords, creating a delicate and refined fragrance.

The base is warm and enveloping, in a symphony of perfect and harmonious accords of musk and noble woods. Sandalwood, cedar and guaiac woods; Together with vanilla and amber, and balsamic accords, they provide a creamy and comfortable touch and at the same time also impart depth and elegance to the composition.

Substantivity on my skin reaches 10 hours with moderate to gentle diffusion.

It is not a fragrance for all tastes, but for lovers of aldehydic compositions, at their best!

DIA is a heavenly fragrance, for women with class and style.

He is the perfect complement to Gold, her nocturnal sister. If DIA were the sun,🌞 GOLD would be the moon.🌚

Enrium 04/09/22 07:32

I was very excited to try Dia. As a fan of both Amouage and Jean-Claude Ellena, I felt that Dia would be a match made in heaven. However, upon trying it, I am underwhelmed. While Dia is a very nice aldehydic floral, competently put together with high quality ingredients, it is nothing special. I'm in agreement with LeSucreRose below: Chanel No. 5 does the same thing, but you get more bang for your buck. Nobody creates barely-there perfumes quite like M. Ellena, and Dia certainly adheres to his signature olfactory watercolour style, but it is ultimately overpriced for what it is. Nonetheless, Dia is like a lighter version of Gold, as was intended, and is a pleasant, elegant day scent.

Dia opens with bright, soapy aldehydes, as clean and radiant as in White Linen. Soft floral notes begin to creep in, notably powdery violet and some clean cyclamen. My dad grows cyclamens, and I love when they feature as a note in perfumery. Softly green and herbal, yet soapy and floral, the opening is beautiful but fleeting.

As it develops, a powdery bouquet emerges on my skin, led by rose. Orris root enhances the powdery quality, and the blossom notes, especially orange blossom, add a smooth, fruity edge to the florals. It is still light and soapy at this stage, very subtle.

As it dries down, it becomes musky and slightly woody, but remains powdery. Very clean and elegant, it fades fast, becoming a slightly sweet musky-powdery skin scent. Sillage and longevity are moderate at best.

Elegant, airy and clean, Dia strikes the balance perfectly between being no-nonsense yet beautifully refined. The notes are nicely balanced and are put together beautifully. Discreet, feminine sophistication, it is like high-quality French hotel soap in a bottle. Really nice, but given the price point, I would buy Gold and Chanel No. 5 Eau Premiere over this. 3.5/5.

molly1217 01/31/22 23:44

A rich and luxurious pink White Linen. How good Dia smells! A familiar yet unfamiliar scent...
Dia is not an endless bleak desert, not a splendid mosque; it is a garden built around a spring in an oasis, a gift unique to the Sultan's beloved princess.
Amouage has never been short of oriental "flowers blooming" floral fragrances. Dia's style is soft and charming. In terms of atmosphere, it is inferior to Gold; in terms of complexity, Dia is not as vigorous and shocking as Ubar. Dia should be the most "moderate" spirit in the ranks of classical Amouage. At every level of the fragrance, there is just nothing that stands out, and it is not excessive. If you remove the frankincense that is Amouage's signature, and then compare Dia with the traditional French aldehyde flower perfume (Gold), you can find that Dia is completely created by the structure and feeling of the aldehyde flower.
Behind Dia is Jean-Claude Ellena (don't be too surprised). Jean-Claude Ellena not only mixes the light and simple perfumes that the public loves, but also Amouage, a full-bodied and large-volume floral fragrance, which is also a matter of course. The inexperienced perfumer does not grasp it properly, so that all kinds of fragrance materials that can play the main role scramble and trample each other, and cannot be mixed.
I am always impressed by Dia's beauty. Although, I was amazed at how quickly it disappeared on my skin.
It seems that the creative requirements put forward by Amouage, the spice kingdom, cannot be stumped by this seasoned master perfumer.
I know that Amouage Dia is the pinnacle of Jean-Claude Ellena's perfumery career!
Who said Amouage scents couldn't be light and clear? Because of Dia's freshness and cuteness, Dia can stand out on the contrary, letting go of the heavy burden of too many spices.
It shares with other Amouage works the characteristics of grace and richness and rich color saturation.
Cedarwood, violets and lemons complete Dia's clean, cool and stimulating start.
As soon as the top note of Dia begins to show, the frankincense at the bottom escapes the musk that coexists with it, surpasses the aldehydes, and stands out before the flowers. Iris and Turkish rose, peony concurrently, aldehydes, complex floral melody of fat powder, because the raw materials are full of light and graceful.
The base notes usher in soft musk sandalwood, the texture of Dia is firm, and the floral aroma is so well-proportioned and rich, smooth and silky. Dia, must be called Fugui!

bibibling 03/16/19 09:31

In the photos this looks like a golden brown color but in reality the one I have is a clear glass with a pale yellow liquid inside. Mine is the one with the rose gold logo/hardware and Amouage written in white lettering and does not say the name "Dia" on the sides like some of the other batches do. I'm just mentioning it because Dia's bottles have changes slightly throughout the years and I'm not sure what year mine is from.

Anyway, if I can describe this in one word, it's ALDEHYDES!!! Whoaaa!!! I did not expect the aldehydes to be this strong! To me, this feels like a Chloe base (peony + rose + white flowers + wood) with an extremely generous blend of aldehydes.

I see the comparisons to Caleche/Climat/No5 and yes, because of the Aldehydes, yes, definitely, but we have to remember that Climat is Aldehydes + Narcissus + LOTV, Caleche and No5 are Aldehydes + Ylang + Iris. Dia is Aldehydes with Peony and Rose so no matter how much these frags are similar due to the aldehydes, they are still also very different.

Dia is a very soapy floral and I would say a modern reinterpretation of those classic aldehyde queens. If you love pretty pink frags with rose + peony, this is a 'big girl' version of that genre for sure.

The aldehydes/soapiness calm down after 10 minutes and I do see more of the orris and heliotrope (basically soft sweet powdery purple florals) emerge to harmonize with the rose and peony. This is one of those frags that evolves with time, like a fog of aldehydes slowly drifting away to revel the fresh and pretty flower garden underneath.

Still, this is not going to be for everyone, definitely try before you buy, when I say "ALDEHYDES!!!" I'm not kidding.

Oh wow, Dia Femme. You're like classy, classy sunshine in a bottle. Very retro and definitely very aldehyde heavy on the top. Chanel No. 5? Pfft as if. No offense to fans of No. 5 but if Chanel's classic is the queen of the perfume world, Dia Femme would be empress of the effing solar system. They're in such different ballparks it isn't even funny. I don't know what vintage 5 is like but I've smelled the modern incarnation and it doesn't hold a candle to Dia.

That said, it definitely isn't going to be for everyone. Dia Femme smells, more or less, like the worlds must luxurious soap or laundry product. In other words amazing, but the association is going to be impossible to shake for some. If you don't like soapy scents don't bother sniffing Dia, it just isn't going to do it for you.

On the other hand if you can handle that look forward to the most vivid, spring-like bouquet of florals you've ever set your nose to. A spray of Dia is like an explosion of spring flowers painted in the way only our good friend JCE could manage. It's sweet but not sickly, fresh but not ozonic, dense but not muddled, etc. etc. I can't help with identifying individual notes in such a busy composition but if anything I definitely smell peach blossom, orange blossom, and rose with a healthy dose of white musk. Woods become more apparent as time goes on as well. To abuse the over-used expression it's a symphony of a fragrance, many players contributing to one beautiful whole.

Longevity is impressive, lasting a full 8-10 hours with 2 sprays. Highly recommended to those who don't recoil at the thought of a perfume smelling vintage or 'old'.

Two years ago when I got a voucher to Selfridges for my birthday for £50 there was one thing I knew for certain: the money were going towards a perfume and the perfume had to be Amouage (I need to add: at that time I only knew that Amouage was expensive, exclusive and DIFFERENT). SA showed me Honour, released in 2011 and sprayed on paper with a big smile - lovely white floral (I learnt that day: I don't like 'lovely white florals'). Next one was Reflection - but Reflection was too 'main stream' for me. Then Ciel. I liked Ciel so I sampled it on my wrist. Nice, but something was missing... SA dismissed Gold, Lyric, Memoir, Jubilation 25 and Epic as 'too oriental' for me: blond, fair skin. She spayed Ubar on paper, but I found it too heavy. And then, as if she was saving the best for the end she grabbed Dia and literally made me let her spray my other wrist with a massive smile 'you'll love that one'. I wanted to sniff it immediately but she didn't let me! 'Wait!' She talked about notes (orange blossom and fig making this fragrance special and unique). And then, after about 2-3 minutes she said: 'Now sniff'. So I did. 'And?' she enquired. 'It's... heavy, and totally different, and beautiful!'. She sprayed more on my wrist, and neck, and then she said: 'Now go, smell it after an hour, two, three. You will come back.' I couldn't stop smelling my wrist on the train back home. I was smiling to myself. She was right: I did go back to buy it few days later.
Now: whenever aldehydes are mentioned the perfume that comes to mind immediately is Chanel no5. It's the fizzy, soapy overwhelming top note. But that's exactly where the minimal similarity ends! Dia is nothing like No5. Dia is so much softer, so much more refined than no5. So much more classy and modern. I mentioned that before: I'm not great with notes so I won't even attempt to describe what I smell. But I absolutely love the dry down. It's sensual but not sexual, it's calm but not quiet, it's mysterious and yet you feel like you almost revealing too much. And I have no idea why but to me it smell like 'sunny, bright, hot color white', whatever that means...
I'm so glad I got that voucher two years ago. I'm so glad this SA was so nice, enthusiastic and helpful. And two years later I'm so happy to know all Amouages and have few in my collection :-)

If the person didn't obsess over it, they will for sure like it.

I definitely recommend you visit their store, try the perfume and let the scent linger on you, decide if you wanna get it or not the day after.

Most Popular Negative Reviews

AveParfum 01/19/16 23:55

Dia is beautiful. It is classic French perfume, but at the same time I find it to be modern and the most innocent and youthful of any from this house. The style reminds me of the original Dolce & Gabbana. Not the actual scents themselves, as they are quite different, but they both open like an aldehyde bomb, extremely powdery, a little bubbly...but give it time and it becomes something altogether different.

At first it smells like a bar of powdery rose soap. Even reminds me of Narciso Essence at first. With time it turns into a sweet floral, and peach blossom really stands out. I thought there was peach in the top notes. Dia has a musky, woody base. All traces of powder and aldehydes fade away eventually, and then it smells like fabric softener musk in the best possible sense. The floral aspect begins to seem more like mimosa or even sweet pea blossoms than rose. It's a sweet and clean floral scent.

I love Dia, so I bought myself a nice, big 100 ml bottle.

Nickie 08/21/13 12:45

A pleasant, clean floral for daytime. That's the sum total of excitement it generates for me, sadly.

It sits close to my skin but, unlike other Amouage experiences, I don't think it'll linger much longer than 3 hours which is a disappointment. (Others have lasted between 7-14 hours.)

Floral/ aldehyde lovers can do a lot worse - but, expense wise, they'd be advised to shop around before investing in what is, frankly, a generic and somewhat dull fragrance.

Andrina72 04/29/18 12:05

There's something sharp here that's almost burning my nose. I'm quite torn about because overall it's quite nice. A VERY BIG powdery floral... which would normally be right up my alley, but there's something in there that stings my nose.

It's probably way over the top for a lot of people. I don't really think it's all that wearable in this day and age when so many people are sensitive about perfumes. The sillage & longevity make it best suited to either staying home or visits with other perfume enthusiasts.

So to recap... smells nice, but burns my nose.... sillage & longevity excellent, which renders it not very wearable in public.

bintTapputi 05/08/20 08:33

First wave of the scent: Soapy, clean, classic. It's No 5 toned down. Uninteresting, for me. But as someone who hates No 5, this is certainly a better alternative to that bright aldehyde mixture. It's way more subtle, less harsh and less "aged". This is a modern spin on that kind of fragrance, and for what it is I think it's done well.

The second wave of the fragrance is much more pleasant. When the floral and woody notes take front stage, it shapes into something I personally enjoy a lot more.

Overall though I just find the whole fragrance rather boring. I'll revisit it in the future, as it may just be the weather today that is putting me off. For now it's a 5/10
